title: Tsige Duguma among four Ethiopian athletes to miss World Indoor Championships due to visa issues
content:
Four Ethiopian athletes will miss this weekend’s World Athletics Indoor Championships in Torun, Poland because of visa issues.

This includes 2024 world indoor champion and Olympic 800m silver medalist Tsige Duguma.

A trio of 1,500m runners — Saron Berhe, Haregeweyn Kalayu and Mosisa Siyoum — will also not compete. Ethiopia, historically a hugely successful nation in athletics, will be represented by six athletes: Nigist Getachew (800m), Birke Haylom (1,500m), Getnet Wale, Addisu Yihune, Freweyni Hailu and Aleshign Baweke (all 3,000m).

A spokesperson for World Athletics told The Athletic: “We can confirm that a very small number of athletes from the Ethiopian federation encountered Visa issues to enter Poland.

“We have been working closely with the Local Organising Committee and government authorities to find resolutions where possible; however, Visa issues may arise for a range of reasons, and immigration is a national responsibility and outside of our remit.”

This is the second time this year that Ethiopian athletes have been prevented from competing at an athletics championship due to visa issues. For the 2026 World Cross Country Championships in Tallahassee, United States in January, Ethiopia were unable to enter full men’s and women’s under 20 teams. There were 14 rejected visas for Ethiopian athletes, according to LetsRun.com.

“We encourage member federations to make sure that they recognize that they need to be absolutely on top of the administrative, paperwork and appointments that athletes are making with various post holders and consulates from around the world,” World Athletics president Seb Coe said at the pre-meet press conference in Torun.

“That has challenges because there are countries that don’t always have a post holder of the host nation and they have to travel elsewhere. It’s a global challenge now,” he added, stating that World Athletics have a “full team” helping the U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Committee (USOPC) and other bodies with the world under-20 championships taking place in Eugene, Oregon in August.

The Ethiopian embassy in Poland, and the Polish home affairs ministry have been approached for comment. Coe, in the press conference, said he had found out about the Ethiopians absences just “the other day”.

There have been broader challenges for Ethiopia in recent years. Middle-distance runner Diribe Welteji, the 1,500m world championship silver medalist in 2023, was banned from competing in the 2025 edition in Tokyo because she refused to provide a sample for an out-of-competition test. The 23-year-old was subsequently banned for two years as of this February, after proceedings went to the court of arbitration for sport, and her silver medal from the 2025 world indoor championships has been rescinded.

Additionally, at the start of March, Worth Athletics announced it would not be ratifying five world records set by three Ethiopian athletes in 2023 and 2024. Collectively, Birke Haylom, Melknat Wudu and Medina Eisa had run best-ever performances by under-20 athletes in the mile, 1,500m (indoors), 3,000m (indoors) and twice over 5,000m — Haylom’s 14:23.71s at the 2024 Prefontaine Classic was lowered to 14:21.89s by Eisa in Brussels that September.

However World Athletics found that birth date records had been falsified for all three runners. Eisa, actually born on October 17th 2002, had her birthday listed as January 3rd 2005, meaning she competed (and twice won gold) at two World under-20 championships while ineligible.

“I’m not trying to minimise it, but if you look at the global scheme of things and the challenges, we want every athlete here,” Coe told reporters in Torun. He says part of the solution involves starting the visa process earlier, and that problems with applications have become a global problem in recent years.
